title: perf-bench-scratch-riley-cooper-2026-03-04
content:
Quick scratchpad for today's perf runs: aim to reproduce the regression reported by SRE (higher p99 on 8k context) and try kv-cache + batching/quant combos. Hand notes, rough outputs, and TODOs below.

Goal:
- Understand p50/p95/p99 changes on 8k and 4k sequences after kernel change v2.1.
- Validate KV-cache warmup behavior and impact on tail latency at low qps.
- Check batching heuristics (max_batch_size, batch_timeout) for latency vs throughput tradeoff.

Environment:
- branch: serving-runtime/perf-kernel-v2.1
- image: redwood-inference/runtime:2026-03-03-v2.1
- HW: g4dn.12x / 8xA100-80GB (local lab) and staging-dedicated pool (4xH100)
- Model: open-llm/redwood-vicuna-13b-8k (fp16) + int8 quant profile (alpha)
- Client: bench-client v0.9.1 (continuous streaming disabled)

Commands used:
- baseline single request latency (no kv-cache):
  ./bench-client --model redwood-vicuna-13b-8k --seq 8192 --batch 1 --qps 1 --steps 64 --mode latency

- kv-cache warmup test (200 identical prompts):
  ./bench-client --model redwood-vicuna-13b-8k --seq 8192 --batch 1 --qps 0.2 --repeats 200 --kv-cache enabled

- batching sweep (max_batch_size, batch_timeout ms):
  for b in 1 2 4 8 16; do for t in 5 10 25 50; do ./bench-client --batch $b --batch_timeout $t --qps 50 --duration 300; done; done

Key config points I changed today:
- kernel selection: enable new attention fusion (flag: --kernel-fusion on)
- kv-cache policy: aggressive prefix caching (policy=v2, ttl=600s)
- quant: int8 run enabled with fallback to fp16 for attention (flag --quant=auto)

Raw-ish outputs (snippets):
- Baseline single-run (g4dn, fp16, no-kv):
  p50: 210ms, p95: 420ms, p99: 980ms, mean: 240ms, tokens/s: 85

- After kernel-v2.1 (same hw):
  p50: 195ms, p95: 400ms, p99: 1200ms (!! spike), mean: 230ms, tokens/s: 92
  -> p99 increased despite improvements at p50/p95. Suspicious tail event(s).

- KV-cache warmup (200 repeats, qps=0.2):
  First 10 requests: avg latency 1.1s (cold decode), after 30th request: avg 240ms, steady-state 220ms.
  Observed occasional 1.5s outliers around requests 87 and 143.

- Batching sweep (qps=50, 4xA100 staging): summary table (manual notes):
  max_batch=1, timeout=5ms -> p95 450ms, throughput 18k tokens/s
  max_batch=4, timeout=10ms -> p95 520ms, throughput 62k tokens/s
  max_batch=8, timeout=25ms -> p95 700ms, throughput 110k tokens/s
  max_batch=16, timeout=50ms -> p95 1.2s, throughput 140k tokens/s (great throughput, bad tail)

Quick hypotheses/observations:
- Kernel v2.1 likely introduced a corner-case in attention fusion that occasionally falls back to a slower codepath (explains p99 spike). Need to check logs for fallback reasons (mem pressure / CUDA kernel launch error).
- KV-cache warmup reduces median latency dramatically but doesn't fix tail outliers; outliers correlate with GC-like events (observed short memory reclaim logs).
- Large batches push throughput up but increase p95/p99; for customer SLOs we need an SLO-aware batching policy (limit max_batch when qps low or when request deadlines tight).

Immediate follow-ups (TODO):
- [ ] Re-run kernel-v2.1 with debug logging enabled (env REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1) and capture CUDA error/fallback traces.
- [ ] Add perf counters around memory alloc/free to correlate with KV-cache outliers.
- [ ] Run more long-duration (1h) low-qps kv-cache test to see frequency of 1.xs outliers.
- [ ] Try disabling attention fusion selectively to confirm p99 regression root cause.
- [ ] Share snippet and ask SRE if the production traces show same pattern (tagging Jordan).

Notes for Jordan/Sam:
- Jordan: can you attach the staging node /var/log/runtime/* around 2026-03-04T09:10Z? I saw outliers at ~09:07 and ~09:42 UTC.
- Sam: please try the same batching sweep on the H100 pool (we only did A100 in staging); curious if kernel fallback happens less on H100.

Misc quick ideas (brainstorm):
- Adaptive batch cutoff: if p95 over window > threshold, temporarily cap max_batch to lower value. Simple control loop in router.
- Hybrid quant fallback: route requests likely to trigger tail events to fp16 model; lighter requests to int8. Need estimator for "tail risk" (sequence length, token distribution).

Links/refs:
- GH PR that introduced kernel change: GH-PR-8123
- Confluence run notes: CONFLUENCE-Perf-Run-2026
- JIRA issue for prod p99: JIRA-RUN-4021

End of notes. These are messy; will clean up after reproducer + debug logs attached.
summary: Scratchpad: perf runs for kernel-v2.1 showing p99 regression on 8k, kv-cache warmup reduces median but tail persists; batching increases throughput at cost of tail latency. Next: enable kernel debug, correlate memory logs, repeat on H100.
